quizzes.question_text: Subtract. You do not need to simplify your answer. $\\[1em]$ $\frac{7}{10}-\frac{1}{2} =$
solution: You can use 10 as the common denominator.

With 10 as the common denominator, we need the fraction $\frac{1}{2}$ to have a denominator of 10. So multiply the numerator and denominator by 5 to find an equivalent fraction. $\frac{1 \times 5}{2 \times 5} = \frac{5}{10}$

Now subtract the fractions. Subtract the numerators and keep the denominators the same. $\frac{7}{10} - \frac{5}{10} = \frac{2}{10}$. You do not have to simplify, but it can be simplified to $\frac{1}{5}$
